Only edit the single DUT. After edit_dut, request verify_rtl before another edit. The registered test_suite_id equals task.id. Only the host determines PASS. Never access files, shell, DPI, includes, hierarchy outside the DUT or change trusted assets. Pure computation system functions allowed: $clog2, $bits, $signed, $unsigned. No preprocessor directives. Fix all defects you identify; do not preserve bugs to force extra rounds.

{"task":{"id":"Prob137_fsm_serial","spec":"
I would like you to implement a module named TopModule with the following
interface. All input and output ports are one bit unless otherwise
specified.

 - input  clk
 - input  reset
 - input  in
 - output done

In many (older) serial communications protocols, each data byte is sent
along with a start bit and a stop bit, to help the receiver delimit bytes
from the stream of bits. One common scheme is to use one start bit (0), 8
data bits, and 1 stop bit (1). The line is also at logic 1 when nothing
is being transmitted (idle).

Implement a finite state machine that will identify when bytes have been
correctly received when given a stream of bits. It needs to identify the
start bit, wait for all 8 data bits, then verify that the stop bit was
correct. If the stop bit does not appear when expected, the FSM must wait
until it finds a stop bit before attempting to receive the next byte.
Include a active-high synchronous reset. Note that the serial protocol
sends the least significant bit first.

Assume all sequential logic is triggered on the positive edge of the
clock.

Inline all helper logic inside TopModule; do not define auxiliary modules. xczu3eg-sbva484-1-e; 5 ns synthesis clock; simulator seed 1. No reference dependencies, hierarchy outside the DUT, file access, includes or DPI."},"current":{"revision_id":"b44f2d2f-a14f-4f52-b349-3b0bdc9f01e0","source_sha256":"cdae6711443582e44eee2fcb6b59ffa95c708a4124a9217ce23768f61bbedc76","source":"
module TopModule (
    input  clk,
    input  reset,
    input  in,
    output done
);

    localparam IDLE = 2'd0,
               DATA = 2'd1,
               STOP = 2'd2,
               WAIT = 2'd3;

    reg [1:0] state;
    reg [2:0] bit_cnt;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state   <= IDLE;
            bit_cnt <= 3'd0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (in == 1'b0) begin
                        state   <= DATA;
                        bit_cnt <= 3'd0;
                    end
                end
                DATA: begin
                    if (bit_cnt == 3'd7) begin
                        state   <= STOP;
                        bit_cnt <= 3'd0;
                    end else begin
                        bit_cnt <= bit_cnt + 3'd1;
                    end
                end
                STOP: begin
                    if (in == 1'b1)
                        state <= IDLE;
                    else
                        state <= WAIT;
                end
                WAIT: begin
                    if (in == 1'b1)
                        state <= IDLE;
                end
                default: state <= IDLE;
            endcase
        end
    end

    assign done = (state == STOP) && in;

endmodule
